content.title: TypeScript is a feedback system
content.text:
For this course, use this simple model:

**You write code → TypeScript checks your assumptions → you fix mismatches → JavaScript can run later.**

The type checker is not predicting every runtime failure. It is checking a particular class of mistakes: whether the code's stated and inferred types fit together.

That distinction matters.

A type error is not the same thing as a runtime error. A program can pass type checking and still contain a logic bug. A program can also fail type checking because your code makes an assumption that the type system cannot prove is safe.

options.text: The function stopped being a function.
The function's parameter contract stayed the same, but the caller stopped matching it.
TypeScript automatically changed `"20"` into a number and changed the function type.

feedback.correct: The function still expects two numbers. The caller supplied a number and a string, so the call no longer matches the function's contract.
feedback.incorrect: The function still expects two numbers. The caller supplied a number and a string, so the call no longer matches the function's contract.

content.title: Why the extra information matters
content.text:
Compare these two lines:

```ts
const total = 125;
```

and

```ts
const total: number = 125;
```

Both communicate that `total` is a number. TypeScript can often discover the first one without an annotation.

That leads to an important habit for this module:

**Do not add type syntax just because you can. Add it when it communicates useful intent or when the checker needs help.**

content.question: Which statement best describes TypeScript's role?

options.text: It replaces JavaScript completely and runs by itself.
It lets you describe and check assumptions about values and program structure before runtime.
It guarantees that a program has no bugs.
It is only a formatting system for code.

feedback.correct: TypeScript improves the information available during development. It does not prove the program is correct in every way.
feedback.incorrect: TypeScript improves the information available during development. It does not prove the program is correct in every way.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Types are information about what values are supposed to be.
**Senior habit:** Treat type errors as evidence about an assumption in your code, not as insults from the compiler.
